Question: May challenge: During summer bridge and next-session readiness, a Class 9 learner is reviewing Matter in Our Surroundings. which statement best describes diffusion in gases?

Subject: Science (086)
Question: May challenge: During summer bridge and next-session readiness, a Class 9 learner is reviewing Matter in Our Surroundings. during melting, the temperature of pure ice at its melting point remains constant because the supplied heat is used to:

Subject: Science (086)
Question: May challenge: During summer bridge and next-session readiness, a Class 9 learner is reviewing Is Matter Around Us Pure. which method is most suitable for separating cream from milk?

Subject: Science (086)
Question: May challenge: During summer bridge and next-session readiness, a Class 9 learner is reviewing Is Matter Around Us Pure. a solution contains 20 g salt in 180 g water. What is its mass percentage of salt?
Explanation: Mass percentage = 20/(20+180) × 100 = 10%.

Subject: Science (086)
Question: May challenge: During summer bridge and next-session readiness, a Class 9 learner is reviewing Atoms and Molecules. what is the chemical formula of aluminium oxide?

Subject: Science (086)
Question: May challenge: During summer bridge and next-session readiness, a Class 9 learner is reviewing Atoms and Molecules. how many molecules are present in 18 g of water?
Explanation: 18 g water is one mole, containing Avogadro’s number of molecules.

Subject: Science (086)
Question: May challenge: During summer bridge and next-session readiness, a Class 9 learner is reviewing Structure of the Atom. which subatomic particle has no electric charge?
Explanation: A neutron is electrically neutral.

Subject: Science (086)
Question: May challenge: During summer bridge and next-session readiness, a Class 9 learner is reviewing Structure of the Atom. an atom has atomic number 17 and mass number 35. Number of neutrons is:
Explanation: Neutrons = mass number − atomic number = 35 − 17 = 18.

Subject: Science (086)
Question: May challenge: During summer bridge and next-session readiness, a Class 9 learner is reviewing The Fundamental Unit of Life. which cell organelle is the main site of aerobic respiration?
Explanation: Mitochondria release usable energy through aerobic cellular respiration.

Subject: Science (086)
Question: May challenge: During summer bridge and next-session readiness, a Class 9 learner is reviewing The Fundamental Unit of Life. a plant cell placed in a concentrated salt solution shrinks away from its cell wall. This is:
Explanation: Water leaves the cell by osmosis, causing the protoplast to shrink.

Subject: Science (086)
Question: May challenge: During summer bridge and next-session readiness, a Class 9 learner is reviewing Tissues. which plant tissue transports water and minerals from roots?
Explanation: Xylem conducts water and dissolved minerals, mainly upward.

Subject: Science (086)
Question: May challenge: During summer bridge and next-session readiness, a Class 9 learner is reviewing Tissues. which feature makes cardiac muscle suitable for continuous rhythmic activity?
Explanation: Intercalated discs connect cardiac cells and support coordinated contraction.

Subject: Science (086)
Question: May challenge: During summer bridge and next-session readiness, a Class 9 learner is reviewing Motion. the slope of a distance-time graph represents:
Explanation: Distance travelled per unit time is speed; it is the graph’s slope.

Subject: Science (086)
Question: May challenge: During summer bridge and next-session readiness, a Class 9 learner is reviewing Force and Laws of Motion. a 2 kg object accelerates at 3 m/s². The net force is:
Explanation: Newton’s second law: F = ma = 2 × 3 = 6 N.

Subject: Science (086)
Question: May challenge: During summer bridge and next-session readiness, a Class 9 learner is reviewing Gravitation. if the distance between two masses is doubled, their gravitational force becomes:
Explanation: Gravitational force varies inversely with the square of distance.

Subject: Science (086)
Question: May challenge: During summer bridge and next-session readiness, a Class 10 learner is reviewing Chemical Reactions and Equations. which observation most directly indicates formation of a gas when zinc reacts with dilute hydrochloric acid?
Explanation: Zinc reacts with dilute HCl to release hydrogen gas, seen as effervescence.

Subject: Science (086)
Question: May challenge: During summer bridge and next-session readiness, a Class 10 learner is reviewing Chemical Reactions and Equations. in the reaction CuO + H2 → Cu + H2O, which substance is reduced?
Explanation: CuO loses oxygen and is reduced to copper.

Subject: Science (086)
Question: May challenge: During summer bridge and next-session readiness, a Class 10 learner is reviewing Acids, Bases and Salts. which indicator turns red in an acidic solution and blue in a basic solution?
Explanation: Litmus is red in acid and blue in base.

Subject: Science (086)
Question: May challenge: During summer bridge and next-session readiness, a Class 10 learner is reviewing Acids, Bases and Salts. a solution has pH 3. Its hydrogen ion concentration compared with pH 5 is:
Explanation: Each pH unit represents a tenfold change; two units means 100 times.

Subject: Science (086)
Question: May challenge: During summer bridge and next-session readiness, a Class 10 learner is reviewing Metals and Non-metals. which metal is commonly stored under kerosene because it reacts vigorously with air and water?
Explanation: Sodium is highly reactive and is stored under kerosene to prevent contact with air/moisture.

Subject: Science (086)
Question: May challenge: During summer bridge and next-session readiness, a Class 10 learner is reviewing Metals and Non-metals. which method is generally used to extract a highly reactive metal such as sodium from its compound?
Explanation: Highly reactive metals are obtained by electrolytic reduction of molten compounds.

Subject: Science (086)
Question: May challenge: During summer bridge and next-session readiness, a Class 10 learner is reviewing Carbon and Its Compounds. the functional group present in ethanol is:
Explanation: Ethanol is an alcohol containing the hydroxyl group.

Subject: Science (086)
Question: May challenge: During summer bridge and next-session readiness, a Class 10 learner is reviewing Carbon and Its Compounds. which pair represents a homologous series?
Explanation: Successive members of an alkane series differ by –CH2–.

Subject: Science (086)
Question: May challenge: During summer bridge and next-session readiness, a Class 10 learner is reviewing Life Processes. which part of the nephron filters blood under pressure?
Explanation: The glomerulus filters blood into Bowman’s capsule.

Subject: Science (086)
Question: May challenge: During summer bridge and next-session readiness, a Class 10 learner is reviewing Life Processes. in humans, most absorption of digested food occurs in the:
Explanation: The small intestine has villi that provide a large absorptive surface.

Subject: Science (086)
Question: May challenge: During summer bridge and next-session readiness, a Class 10 learner is reviewing Control and Coordination. which part of the brain maintains posture and balance?
Explanation: The cerebellum coordinates muscular activity, posture and balance.

Subject: Science (086)
Question: May challenge: During summer bridge and next-session readiness, a Class 10 learner is reviewing Control and Coordination. a plant shoot bends towards light because auxin:
Option A: Accumulates on illuminated side and stops growth
Option B: Accumulates on shaded side and promotes elongation
Explanation: Auxin promotes greater cell elongation on the shaded side, bending the shoot towards light.

Subject: Science (086)
Question: May challenge: During summer bridge and next-session readiness, a Class 10 learner is reviewing How Do Organisms Reproduce?. which process produces genetically identical offspring in Amoeba?
Explanation: Amoeba commonly reproduces asexually by binary fission.

Subject: Science (086)
Question: May challenge: During summer bridge and next-session readiness, a Class 10 learner is reviewing Heredity. in a cross Tt × Tt, where T is dominant, what fraction of offspring is expected to be tt?
Explanation: The genotype ratio is 1 TT : 2 Tt : 1 tt, so one-fourth are tt.

Subject: Science (086)
Question: May challenge: During summer bridge and next-session readiness, a Class 10 learner is reviewing Light – Reflection and Refraction. an object is placed beyond 2F of a convex lens. The image is:
Explanation: For an object beyond 2F, a convex lens forms a real, inverted, diminished image between F and 2F.

Question: May challenge: During summer bridge and next-session readiness, a Class 9 learner is reviewing Quadrilaterals. the sum of interior angles of a quadrilateral is:
Explanation: A quadrilateral can be divided into two triangles; total = 2 × 180°.

Question: May challenge: During summer bridge and next-session readiness, a Class 9 learner is reviewing Areas of Parallelograms and Triangles. parallelograms on the same base and between the same parallels have:
Explanation: They have the same base and height, so their areas are equal.

Subject: Mathematics Standard (041)
Question: May challenge: During summer bridge and next-session readiness, a Class 9 learner is reviewing Circles. the perpendicular from the centre of a circle to a chord:
Explanation: A perpendicular from the centre to a chord bisects the chord.

Question: May challenge: During summer bridge and next-session readiness, a Class 10 learner is reviewing Some Applications of Trigonometry. the angle of elevation to the top of a tower increases while the observer moves closer. The tower height is unchanged. The horizontal distance:

Subject: Mathematics Standard (041)
Question: May challenge: During summer bridge and next-session readiness, a Class 10 learner is reviewing Circles. a tangent to a circle is perpendicular to the radius at the:
Explanation: The radius drawn to the point of contact is perpendicular to the tangent.

Subject: Mathematics Standard (041)
Question: May challenge: During summer bridge and next-session readiness, a Class 10 learner is reviewing Areas Related to Circles. area of a 90° sector of a circle of radius 14 cm (π=22/7) is:
Explanation: Sector area = 90/360 × πr² = 1/4 × 616 = 154 cm².

Subject: Mathematics Standard (041)
Question: May challenge: During summer bridge and next-session readiness, a Class 10 learner is reviewing Surface Areas and Volumes. a cylinder has radius 3 cm and height 5 cm. Its volume is:
Explanation: Volume = πr²h = π×9×5 = 45π cm³.

Subject: Mathematics Standard (041)
Question: May challenge: During summer bridge and next-session readiness, a Class 10 learner is reviewing Statistics. for a frequency distribution, the class mark of 20–30 is:
Explanation: Class mark is the midpoint: (20+30)/2 = 25.

Subject: Mathematics Standard (041)
Question: May challenge: During summer bridge and next-session readiness, a Class 10 learner is reviewing Probability. a card is drawn from a well-shuffled deck of 52 cards. Probability of drawing an ace is:
Explanation: There are four aces among 52 cards; 4/52 = 1/13.

Subject: Mathematics Standard (041)
Question: May challenge: During summer bridge and next-session readiness, a Class 10 learner is reviewing Applications of Quadratic Equations. a rectangle has area 48 cm² and length 2 cm more than breadth. Its breadth is:
Explanation: Let breadth b; b(b+2)=48 gives b²+2b−48=0, so b=6 (positive root).

Subject: Social Science (087)
Question: May challenge: During summer bridge and next-session readiness, a Class 9 learner is reviewing The French Revolution. which estate in pre-revolutionary France paid most of the taxes?

Subject: Social Science (087)
Question: May challenge: During summer bridge and next-session readiness, a Class 9 learner is reviewing The French Revolution. the Tennis Court Oath was taken to demand:

Subject: Social Science (087)

Subject: Social Science (087)
Question: May challenge: During summer bridge and next-session readiness, a Class 9 learner is reviewing India – Size and Location. the Standard Meridian of India is:

Subject: Social Science (087)

Explanation: The Himalayas are geologically young fold mountains.

Subject: Social Science (087)
Question: May challenge: During summer bridge and next-session readiness, a Class 9 learner is reviewing Drainage. which river is an example of a river flowing through a rift valley?
Explanation: The Narmada flows westward through a rift valley.

Subject: Social Science (087)
Question: May challenge: During summer bridge and next-session readiness, a Class 9 learner is reviewing Climate. the southwest monsoon normally reaches Kerala in:
Explanation: The southwest monsoon usually arrives over Kerala around the beginning of June.

Subject: Social Science (087)
Question: May challenge: During summer bridge and next-session readiness, a Class 9 learner is reviewing Natural Vegetation and Wildlife. tropical evergreen forests are generally found in areas with:
Explanation: High rainfall and warmth support dense evergreen vegetation.

Subject: Social Science (087)
Question: May challenge: During summer bridge and next-session readiness, a Class 9 learner is reviewing Population. the number of persons living per unit area is called:
Explanation: Population density is commonly expressed as persons per square kilometre.

Subject: Social Science (087)
Question: May challenge: During summer bridge and next-session readiness, a Class 9 learner is reviewing What is Democracy?. which feature is essential to democracy?
Explanation: Democracy rests on rulers being elected by the people.

Subject: Social Science (087)
Question: May challenge: During summer bridge and next-session readiness, a Class 9 learner is reviewing Constitutional Design. apartheid was a system of:
Explanation: Apartheid enforced racial segregation and discrimination in South Africa.

Subject: Social Science (087)
Question: May challenge: During summer bridge and next-session readiness, a Class 9 learner is reviewing Electoral Politics. in India, elections to the Lok Sabha are generally held every:
Explanation: The normal term of the Lok Sabha is five years unless dissolved earlier.

Subject: Social Science (087)
Question: May challenge: During summer bridge and next-session readiness, a Class 9 learner is reviewing People as Resource. investment in education and health helps create:
Explanation: Education and health improve people’s skills, productivity and capabilities.

Subject: Social Science (087)
Question: May challenge: During summer bridge and next-session readiness, a Class 9 learner is reviewing Poverty as a Challenge. the poverty line is used primarily to estimate:
Option B: Minimum consumption/income needed for basic needs
Explanation: The poverty line identifies a minimum level needed to meet basic requirements.

Subject: Social Science (087)
Chapter: The Rise of Nationalism in Europe
Topic: The Rise of Nationalism in Europe
Question: May challenge: During summer bridge and next-session readiness, a Class 10 learner is reviewing The Rise of Nationalism in Europe. who is associated with the policy of blood and iron in German unification?
Explanation: Bismarck used a policy of military strength and diplomacy to unify Germany.

Subject: Social Science (087)
Question: May challenge: During summer bridge and next-session readiness, a Class 10 learner is reviewing Nationalism in India. the Non-Cooperation Movement was withdrawn after:
Explanation: The violent incident at Chauri Chaura in 1922 led Gandhi to withdraw the movement.

Subject: Social Science (087)
Chapter: The Making of a Global World
Topic: The Making of a Global World
Question: May challenge: During summer bridge and next-session readiness, a Class 10 learner is reviewing The Making of a Global World. the Silk Routes connected Asia with:
Explanation: Silk Routes linked Asian regions with Europe and North Africa through trade and cultural exchange.

Subject: Social Science (087)
Chapter: Print Culture and the Modern World
Topic: Print Culture and the Modern World
Question: May challenge: During summer bridge and next-session readiness, a Class 10 learner is reviewing Print Culture and the Modern World. the first printing press in Europe is associated with:
Explanation: Gutenberg developed a movable-type printing press in Europe in the fifteenth century.

Subject: Social Science (087)
Question: May challenge: During summer bridge and next-session readiness, a Class 10 learner is reviewing Resources and Development. which soil is especially suitable for cotton cultivation?
Explanation: Black soil retains moisture and is well suited to cotton.

Subject: Social Science (087)
Question: May challenge: During summer bridge and next-session readiness, a Class 10 learner is reviewing Forest and Wildlife Resources. a species found only in a particular geographical area is called:
Explanation: Endemic species are restricted to a specific region.

Subject: Social Science (087)
Question: May challenge: During summer bridge and next-session readiness, a Class 10 learner is reviewing Water Resources. which is a major purpose of rainwater harvesting?
Explanation: Harvesting stores rainwater and helps replenish groundwater.

Subject: Social Science (087)
Question: May challenge: During summer bridge and next-session readiness, a Class 10 learner is reviewing Agriculture. rabi crops are generally sown in:
Explanation: Rabi crops such as wheat are sown in winter and harvested in spring.

Subject: Social Science (087)
Question: May challenge: During summer bridge and next-session readiness, a Class 10 learner is reviewing Minerals and Energy Resources. which of the following is a non-conventional source of energy?
Explanation: Solar energy is renewable and classed as a non-conventional source.

Subject: Social Science (087)
Question: May challenge: During summer bridge and next-session readiness, a Class 10 learner is reviewing Manufacturing Industries. the main reason iron and steel is called a basic industry is that it:
Option B: Supplies inputs to many other industries
Explanation: Iron and steel provide essential inputs for machinery, construction and other industries.

Subject: Social Science (087)
Question: May challenge: During summer bridge and next-session readiness, a Class 10 learner is reviewing Power Sharing. power sharing among legislature, executive and judiciary is called:
Explanation: Horizontal power sharing distributes authority among organs at the same level.

Subject: Social Science (087)
Question: May challenge: During summer bridge and next-session readiness, a Class 10 learner is reviewing Federalism. which subject is generally included in the Union List in India?
Explanation: Defence is a Union subject.

Subject: Social Science (087)
Question: May challenge: During summer bridge and next-session readiness, a Class 10 learner is reviewing Gender, Religion and Caste. a belief that one religion is superior and should dominate politics is associated with:
Explanation: Communalism uses religious identity to promote political dominance or division.

Subject: Social Science (087)
Question: May challenge: During summer bridge and next-session readiness, a Class 10 learner is reviewing Political Parties. a major function of political parties is to:
Explanation: Political parties nominate candidates, contest elections and organise government.

Subject: Social Science (087)
Question: May challenge: During summer bridge and next-session readiness, a Class 10 learner is reviewing Development. why is per capita income alone an incomplete measure of development?
Option B: It ignores health, education and distribution
Explanation: Development also depends on quality of life and how income is distributed.

Subject: English Language & Literature (184)
Question: May challenge: During summer bridge and next-session readiness, a Class 9 learner is reviewing Reading Comprehension. in an unseen passage, the central idea is best identified by:
Option B: Finding the main point supported by the passage
Explanation: The central idea is the main message developed across the passage.

Subject: English Language & Literature (184)
Question: May challenge: During summer bridge and next-session readiness, a Class 9 learner is reviewing Reading Comprehension. if a passage says a measure “mitigated” a problem, mitigated most nearly means:
Explanation: Mitigate means to make something less severe.

Subject: English Language & Literature (184)
Question: May challenge: During summer bridge and next-session readiness, a Class 9 learner is reviewing Grammar – Tenses. choose the correct verb: “She ____ to school every day.”
Explanation: A singular third-person subject takes “goes” in the simple present.

Subject: English Language & Literature (184)
Question: May challenge: During summer bridge and next-session readiness, a Class 9 learner is reviewing Grammar – Modals. “You ____ wear a helmet while riding a motorcycle.”
Explanation: Must expresses strong obligation or necessity.

Subject: English Language & Literature (184)
Question: May challenge: During summer bridge and next-session readiness, a Class 9 learner is reviewing Grammar – Subject Verb Agreement. choose the correct sentence.
Option A: The list of items are long.
Option B: The list of items is long.
Option C: The list of items were long.
Option D: The list of items have long.
Explanation: The subject is singular “list”; the phrase “of items” does not change its number.

Subject: English Language & Literature (184)
Question: May challenge: During summer bridge and next-session readiness, a Class 9 learner is reviewing Writing – Descriptive Paragraph. a descriptive paragraph should primarily use:
Option A: Relevant sensory details and precise language
Explanation: Description is strengthened by specific details and coherent organisation.

Subject: English Language & Literature (184)
Question: May challenge: During summer bridge and next-session readiness, a Class 9 learner is reviewing Writing – Diary Entry. which feature is most appropriate for a diary entry?
Explanation: Diary entries usually express the writer’s personal experiences and feelings.

Subject: English Language & Literature (184)
Question: May challenge: During summer bridge and next-session readiness, a Class 9 learner is reviewing Literature – Prose. when analysing a character, the strongest evidence is:
Option B: Actions, dialogue and choices in the text
Explanation: Character traits should be inferred from textual evidence.

Subject: English Language & Literature (184)
Question: May challenge: During summer bridge and next-session readiness, a Class 9 learner is reviewing Literature – Poetry. a comparison using “like” or “as” is a:
Explanation: A simile explicitly compares two things using like or as.

Subject: English Language & Literature (184)
Question: May challenge: During summer bridge and next-session readiness, a Class 9 learner is reviewing Literature – Poetry. repeated initial consonant sounds in nearby words are called:
Explanation: Alliteration is repetition of initial consonant sounds.

Subject: English Language & Literature (184)
Question: May challenge: During summer bridge and next-session readiness, a Class 9 learner is reviewing Vocabulary in Context. the antonym of “scarce” is:
Explanation: Abundant means plentiful, the opposite of scarce.

Subject: English Language & Literature (184)
Question: May challenge: During summer bridge and next-session readiness, a Class 9 learner is reviewing Grammar – Determiners. choose the correct determiner: “There is ____ milk left, enough for one cup.”
Explanation: Milk is uncountable; “a little” refers to a small amount.

Subject: English Language & Literature (184)
Question: May challenge: During summer bridge and next-session readiness, a Class 9 learner is reviewing Grammar – Reported Speech. direct: He said, “I am tired.” Choose the correct reported form.
Option A: He said that he is tired.
Option B: He said that he was tired.
Option C: He says that I was tired.
Explanation: With a past reporting verb, present “am” normally backshifts to “was”.

Subject: English Language & Literature (184)
Question: May challenge: During summer bridge and next-session readiness, a Class 9 learner is reviewing Reading – Inference. a character repeatedly checks the clock before an interview. The most reasonable inference is that the character is:
Option B: Anxious or eager about the interview
Explanation: Repeated clock-checking before an important event suggests anticipation or nervousness.

Subject: English Language & Literature (184)
Question: May challenge: During summer bridge and next-session readiness, a Class 9 learner is reviewing Writing – Formal Letter. which is essential in a formal letter of complaint?
Option B: Clear description of the issue and a reasonable requested action
Explanation: A formal complaint should state facts, impact and the remedy sought.

Subject: English Language & Literature (184)
Question: May challenge: During summer bridge and next-session readiness, a Class 10 learner is reviewing Reading Comprehension. which statement best describes an inference?
Option A: A fact copied word for word
Option B: A conclusion drawn from textual clues
Option D: A personal opinion unrelated to the text
Explanation: An inference is a reasoned conclusion based on evidence and prior understanding.

Subject: English Language & Literature (184)
Question: May challenge: During summer bridge and next-session readiness, a Class 10 learner is reviewing Reading Comprehension. the phrase “the plan was feasible” means the plan was:
Option B: Practical and capable of being carried out
Explanation: Feasible means possible or practical to do.

Subject: English Language & Literature (184)
Question: May challenge: During summer bridge and next-session readiness, a Class 10 learner is reviewing Grammar – Tenses. choose the correct form: “By next Friday, they ____ the project.”
Explanation: Future perfect describes an action completed before a specified future time.

Subject: English Language & Literature (184)
Question: May challenge: During summer bridge and next-session readiness, a Class 10 learner is reviewing Grammar – Modals. “You ____ have informed us earlier; the delay caused difficulty.”
Explanation: Should have expresses an expected action that was not done.

Subject: English Language & Literature (184)
Question: May challenge: During summer bridge and next-session readiness, a Class 10 learner is reviewing Grammar – Reported Speech. direct: Mira said, “I have finished my work.”
Option A: Mira said that she has finished her work.
Option B: Mira said that she had finished her work.
Option C: Mira says she finished my work.
Option D: Mira told that I had finished work.
Explanation: Present perfect generally backshifts to past perfect after a past reporting verb.

Subject: English Language & Literature (184)
Question: May challenge: During summer bridge and next-session readiness, a Class 10 learner is reviewing Grammar – Subject Verb Agreement. choose the correct verb: “Neither the teacher nor the students ____ absent.”
Explanation: With neither…nor, the verb agrees with the nearer subject, “students”.

Subject: English Language & Literature (184)
Question: May challenge: During summer bridge and next-session readiness, a Class 10 learner is reviewing Writing – Analytical Paragraph. when comparing two data sets in an analytical paragraph, the writer should:
Option B: Identify key trends, comparisons and relevant figures
